source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
DataBank's McLean IAD2 campus publishes 3 MW of IT capacity across 40,690 square feet of technical space. That works out to roughly 74 watts per square foot, a density consistent with mixed enterprise and colocation use rather than hyperscale AI training halls. No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so no statement can be made about what compliance frameworks the facility qualifies to host. Tier level, redundancy architecture, and pricing are not published on the operator's spec page.

At a common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 3 MW of IT load would support roughly 75 racks, at 10 kW per rack, a more typical enterprise colocation assumption, the same capacity supports roughly 300 racks. Neither figure is the operator's claim; both are arithmetic translations of the single published number. Three megawatts is a modest envelope by current AI infrastructure standards, where a single large training cluster can consume that entire allocation on its own.

Virginia is the largest data center market in the world by installed capacity, and this site has mapped 326 facilities in the state, of which only 19 publish a megawatt figure. IAD2 ranks 19th out of those 19 by published IT capacity, meaning it sits at the bottom of the published-MW cohort, which together totals 1,326 MW. That ranking reflects the published figure alone and says nothing about facilities that have not disclosed capacity. For a reader evaluating AI infrastructure options in Northern Virginia, IAD2's published scale places it outside the range where large-scale model training or inference clusters are typically housed, though its McLean location, adjacent to the dense Loudoun County corridor, may carry network or compliance value that the published specifications do not capture.
